+# Three staged entries and an LP-exact literal fill
+
+Prepared by Rohan Arun with Anthropic Claude assistance. Apache-2.0. The construction reuses the credited staged-entry,
+frame, owner and admission machinery listed in NOTICE.md.
+
+## 1. Staged entries are exact rewrites, checked as such
+
+Let `h` be an ordinary helper whose entrance frame is `E_h` and whose early reads add `±h/4` into four registers before
+a cut `c`. A staged entry raises the entrance to `E_h + ⟨p⟩`, deletes those reads, and inserts releases after the cut
+that realize the same linear map on every live input and dirty private buffer. In PR3949's construction the release
+vector is `a = M_c v − e_h` with `v = e_h + w`, where `M_c` is the prefix matrix at the cut and `w` is orthogonal to
+every consumer that could still observe it. Releases may land in any register, including another helper; that
+extension is what makes the three entries here possible.
+
+No identity is assumed. Each final word passes:
+
+- PR3734/PR3945 hygiene, including the wrapper rule that no wrapper touches an entering or restored helper;
+- the Lagrangian frame bill equal to its declared report;
+- arbitrary-dirty forward, contragredient and cleanup-boundary semantics (`audit_core`, Sagar Thakrar PR3687);
+- in the admission closure, the whole-word interpreter `audit_verify.semantics`, with 632 live inputs, 91 dirty
+  buffers, a 723-dimensional matrix, reverse pull-back equal to forward and no buffer-to-live leak. Constructive
+  controls must also be rejected: each omitted or sign-flipped release, each old entrance, a wrong bill and a wrong
+  slice preimage, 17 per provider;
+- fresh five-stage native replay: transport, ledgers, local replay, wrappers, and phases with all-column warp recipes.
+
+The edit is finite literal data (`recipe/RECORD-*.json`). The opcode-level contract is checked independently by
+`checks/independent_frames.py`. The B section of each provider loses exactly these twelve reads:
+
+`600 → 183, 202, 175, 123`, `608 → 114, 137, 173, 121` and `609 → 114, 137, 173, 121`, each weighted `±1/4`.
+
+It gains exactly these six releases:
+
+`609 → 121 (+1/2)`, `608 → 137 (−1/2)`, `600 → 202 (−1/2)`, `600 → 602 (−1)`, `608 → 610 (−1)` and `609 → 610 (−1)`.
+
+All other B operators, every A and restore operator, all native lenders and matrices, all returns, ports and removed
+registers are unchanged.
+
+## 2. Local bill
+
+With exact optimal frames (`frames_exact.py`, written back and re-billed by `audit_core.frame_bill`), each provider's
+local profile changes per call by
+
+`ΔL = +6 H1 + 2 H2 + 5 H3 − 7 H4`,
+
+with rank mass `6 + 4 + 15 − 28 = −3`, exactly the three removed width units. Helpers 600, 608 and 609 each go from
+width 8 to width 7, giving inventory `5:28, 6:18, 7:56, 8:93, 9:213`.
+
+## 3. Owner fill attaining the window-free optimum
+
+**Target.** For the new inventory the window-free pattern LP (bins: 241,920 × 8; 161,280 each of 16, 32 and 48)
+attains idle `{3: 23328 − 486, 5: 4320 − 2430, 48: 137952 + 486}`. PR3815's class-level Hall LP, with exact Hall
+conditions per width over every call interval, gives the same optimum on this clock, so the time windows do not bind
+in aggregate. No fill can do better than the window-free LP.
+
+**Integer selection.** Each owner class (owner, capacity, window) keeps PR3945's pattern counts except for:
+
+- exactly 486 changes `(9,9,9,9,9)` → empty in cap-48 bins;
+- exactly 2,430 changes `(9,9,9)+5` → a zero-idle cap-32 pattern;
+- any number of zero-idle → zero-idle changes among the cap-32 patterns `(9,9,9,5), (9,9,8,6), (9,9,7,7), (9,8,8,7),
+  (8,8,8,8)` and the cap-16 patterns `(9,7)` and `(8,8)`.
+
+Per-width global balance is imposed. For every width and every call interval, the slots of classes whose window lies
+inside the interval may not exceed the new per-call supply times its length; this is Hall's condition, necessary and
+sufficient for an interval transport. Rows are separated lazily and the final solution is re-checked exhaustively over
+all 5,250,420 intervals for each width. HiGHS returns an integral selection of 14,904 changed bins in 78 class records (`owner/build/CHANGES.json`).
+
+**Transport.** For each width, every bin owns a fixed number of slots, and each call must receive exactly the new
+per-call count within the bin's owner window. This is an interval transport, solved as a min-cost flow with a segment
+tree over calls: a slot staying at its old call costs 0 and a moved slot costs 1. Same-call collisions inside a bin
+(two widths landing on one call) are repaired by exchanging call times with another bin's slot of the same width.
+Same-family children of an owner have pairwise disjoint windows, which the checker asserts, so per-bin distinctness is
+the full same-call family condition. Helpers are then assigned to slots per call by width, and offsets become compact
+chronological prefixes.
+
+**Result.** 70,876 roles move. `owner/verify.py` (PR3945's walk) checks all 1,321,920 roles in 725,760 bins and
+reproduces the target idle exactly.
+
+## 4. Complete profile and root
+
+Starting from PR3945's complete profile, adding `3240·ΔL` and the idle change `{3: −486, 5: −2430, 48: +486}` (rank
+mass `+9720 = 3·3240`) gives
+
+`8061120 H1 + 2313360 H2 + 745362 H3 + 330480 H4 + 66690 H5 + 25920 H8 + 138438 H48`.
+
+For `T = 360` the normalized moment `F(κ) = Σ_r n_r r (73/r)^κ − 896·360·73` is continuous and strictly increasing,
+since every `r < 73` and every `n_r > 0`. Rational log and exp remainder bounds give `F < 0` at
+`0.001730809033576552081734` and `F > 0` at `0.001730809033576552081735`. The same enclosures certify PR3945's
+bracket `[0.001730663236534549309146, 0.001730663236534549309147]`. The padded endpoint
+`0.001730809033576552081734 − 10^−46 − 10^−70` exceeds PR3945's certified upper bound by more than
+`1.45797042002772587·10^−7`.
+
+## 5. Scope
+
+The new construction is the three staged entries, their exact frames, and the literal fill. Ordinary discovery,
+parent lift, rebinding and outer release are the inherited engines, run end to end on these words and this fill
+(`admission/`). The result stays conditional on the same universal/all-size source, hosting, recovery, tape, precision,
+analytic and BIT hypotheses as PR3945. It establishes no unconditional multitape multiplication exponent, no change to
+the repository's selected frontier, no new Lean theorem, and no independent human review.

+# Three staged helper entries on the PR3945 staged544 supplier
+
+This package stages three more helpers on PR3945's terminal-width5 staged544 words, re-solves the exact frames, and
+builds a new literal T360 owner fill for the narrowed inventory. Helpers 608, 609 and 600 each get one extra entrance
+dimension. Each loses its four early quarter-weight reads, and two exact releases are inserted after a common cut. Each
+of the three helpers then drops from width 8 to width 7. The literal T360 owner fill is rebuilt so the freed width
+lands in larger idle blocks, which gives the window-free pattern-LP optimum for the new inventory. The new complete
+moment root lies in
+
+**[0.001730809033576552081734, 0.001730809033576552081735]**.
+
+The conditional outer endpoint is the lower bound minus `10^−46 + 10^−70`:
+
+`κ = 0.001730809033576552081734 − 10^−46 − 10^−70`,
+
+which is **+1.4579704200277·10^−7 above PR3945** (+0.0084%). It inherits the same source, hosting, analytic and
+multiplication-model hypotheses as PR3945. No unconditional multiplication exponent, selected-frontier change or Lean
+formalization is claimed.
+
+| | PR3945 | this package |
+|---|---|---|
+| local profile per call | `{1:2482, 2:712, 3:218, 4:109, 5:20, 8:8}` | `{1:2488, 2:714, 3:223, 4:102, 5:20, 8:8}` |
+| helper widths 5/6/7/8/9 | 28 / 18 / 53 / 96 / 213 | 28 / 18 / **56 / 93** / 213 |
+| owner idle | `{3:23328, 5:4320, 48:137952}` | `{3:22842, 5:1890, 48:138438}` |
+| complete profile | `{1:8041680, 2:2306880, 3:729648, 4:353160, 5:69120, 8:25920, 48:137952}` | `{1:8061120, 2:2313360, 3:745362, 4:330480, 5:66690, 8:25920, 48:138438}` |
+| root lower bound | 0.001730663236534549309146 | **0.001730809033576552081734** |
+
+## What changed
+
+**Words** (`recipe/`, `inputs/`). Each staged entry follows PR3949's staged-entry construction, extended so that
+releases may land in any register (including other helpers): raise the helper's entrance to a hyperplane-compatible
+frame P, delete its reads before the cut, and insert releases `a = M_c(e_h + w) − e_h`, with `w` in the kernel of every
+later consumer. After all three entries, the exact frame optimum (the repository's `frames_exact.py`) is written back
+into A/B/restore and cleanup is re-derived literally. `recipe/RECORD-*.json` are source-guarded literal records:
+ordered slice preimages, entrance preimages, warp identity/map preservation, and canonical hashes of the source and
+target words. `recipe/staged_entries_applier.py` replays them without any solver. B loses 12 reads and gains 6
+releases. A and restore keep their operator sequences, and returns, ports, removed set and native lenders/matrices are
+unchanged.
+
+| helper | entrance | deleted reads (B) | releases |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 608 | `[45] → [97,45]` | into 114, 137, 173, 121 (±1/4) | −1/2 into 137; −1 into helper 610 |
+| 609 | `[45] → [97,45]` | into 114, 137, 173, 121 (+1/4) | +1/2 into 121; −1 into helper 610 |
+| 600 | `[45] → [127,45]` | into 183, 202, 175, 123 (±1/4) | −1/2 into 202; −1 into helper 602 |
+
+**Owner fill** (`owner/`). The window-free LP and PR3815's class-level Hall LP both give the same optimum for the new
+inventory: 486 more empty cap-48 bins, 2,430 fewer idle-5 bins and 486 fewer idle-3 bins. The obvious repacking is not
+attainable on this clock: every idle-5 bin's window ends by call 265, and 2,493 calls hold all 96 eights in cap-8 bins.
+The fill was built in three steps. First, an integer program chooses per-class zero-idle pattern changes subject to
+exact per-width Hall conditions. Then each width is moved by a min-cost interval transport. Finally, same-call
+collisions are repaired. Relative to PR3945's literal fill, 70,876 of 1,321,920 roles change (owner, child, port).
+`owner/MOVES.json.gz` lists them, and `owner/build_fill.py` regenerates the fill from PR3945's bytes with the standard
+library only.
+
+## Replay
+
+Python 3.12, standard library only, from the repository root:
+
+```sh
+python -B research/staged544-triple-entry-fill/verify.py
+python -B research/staged544-triple-entry-fill/checks/independent_frames.py --controls
+python -B research/staged544-triple-entry-fill/checks/exact_root.py --controls
+python -B research/staged544-triple-entry-fill/owner/verify.py
+python -B research/staged544-triple-entry-fill/owner/build_fill.py
+python -B research/staged544-triple-entry-fill/test_verify.py
+python -O -B research/staged544-triple-entry-fill/test_verify.py
+python -B research/staged544-triple-entry-fill/admission/authenticate.py
+```
+
+- `verify.py` reconstructs both words from PR3945's words and runs hygiene and the Lagrangian frame bill. It also runs
+  the arbitrary-dirty forward, dual and cleanup-boundary semantics of the retained `audit_core`, and authenticates the
+  fresh native receipts.
+- `checks/independent_frames.py` reuses PR3945's standard-library GF(2) walker. It checks the declared deletions,
+  releases and entrances, the profile delta and the inventory, with 10 mutation controls.
+- `checks/exact_root.py` uses rational log/exp enclosures to certify the new root bracket and PR3945's bracket, and
+  shows that the padded endpoint beats PR3945's upper bound (4 controls).
+- `owner/verify.py` runs PR3945's owner walk over every role of both PR3945's fill and the new fill. It checks source
+  windows, family distinctness, compact offsets, capacity, idle and the complete histogram. Controls include restoring
+  any narrowed width, which must overflow an exactly packed bin.
+- `admission/authenticate.py` authenticates the complete inherited ordinary/outer release run described below.
+
+Fresh native phases need NumPy (about 3–6 minutes per word here):
+
+```sh
+python -B research/staged544-triple-entry-fill/native/run_native.py research/staged544-triple-entry-fill/inputs/NEW-base.json.gz new-native-base
+python -B research/staged544-triple-entry-fill/native/run_native.py research/staged544-triple-entry-fill/inputs/NEW-extra.json.gz new-native-extra
+```
+
+Both five-stage runs passed on the exact gzip inputs (`evidence/NATIVE-*.json`).
+
+**Complete admission.** `admission/full_replay.py` rebuilds PR3945's exact 666-file closure from the pinned predecessor
+archive, using PR3945's own terminal generator and source patches. It adds the six staged-entry files (672 total),
+reruns both native providers fresh, and runs the inherited admission engine end to end on these words and this fill.
+That covers owners, parent lift, rebinding, discovery, outer ledger and independent outer check, and release. The only
+engine edits are PR3945's: source-profile commit, manifest and file count, plus frozen-SPEC control counts. The
+retained receipts are in `admission/`.
+
+```sh
+python3.12 -B research/staged544-triple-entry-fill/admission/full_replay.py --work /fresh/external/path
+```
+
+## Credit
+
+The staged-entry mechanism is Ross Richardson's PR3605 (staged entrance, literal cleanup) and dataisfire's PR3734
+(staged544 supplier, retained source closure, `stage544_applier`). The general census and assembler are
+ChaloupeMusic / Erwan Secousses' PR3949, and the attained T360 clock and fill are PR3815, with PR3638 lineage. The
+terminal-width5 words, owner walk, independent frame walker, rational root enclosures, native runner and admission
+adaptation are Dugongue's PR3945. Exact frame solver: Marius-Paul Dumitrean (`rank7-skip-restore-optimum`). Audit core
+and semantics: Sagar Thakrar (PR3687) and roger-sato (PR3693). zxv PR3682 supplies the comparison claim. Independent
+audits of PR3945 by #3969, #3987 and #3994 were read. NOTICE.md lists the full lineage. New staged entries, owner-fill
+construction, checks and integration: prepared by Rohan Arun with Anthropic Claude assistance. Apache-2.0. No
+independent human review is claimed.
+
+## Open next questions
+
+- **A fourth entry?** The window-free LP shows that a fourth 8→7 narrowing loses: k = 4 prices at −9.06·10^−8 because
+  the Y-type eight-slot sinks ((9,8,8,7), (8,8), (8,8,8,8)) give only about 3.33 helpers' worth of capacity. Is there a
+  staged entry with a different width move (9→8, 7→6) or a different sink that still pays?
+- **Other triads.** Helpers 600/601/602 and 608/609/610 form release triads: each release lands in the third member,
+  and only two of a triad stack. Are there more such triads among the remaining width-8 helpers? Start with the
+  general staged-entry search on these words.
+- **Different repack.** The fill realizes the LP optimum, but only after moving 70,876 roles. Is there a smaller move
+  set, or a clock change, that admits a cheaper narrowing schedule?

+Complete admission for the staged-entry derivative (helpers 608, 609, 600)
+
+full_replay.py extends PR3945's admission/full_replay.py. It downloads (or takes via --archive) the pinned
+predecessor archive (research/staged544-producer-return/REPLAY-INPUTS.tar.gz at fa041037, 756 members checked).
+It then reconstructs PR3945's exact 666-file closure, asserting PR3945's manifest
+3d2ee0175b0cd8aec80c12fef82c2da3a3a54785ca9113140762fd5c41979608, using PR3945's own terminal applier and review
+and its three literal source patches (byte-identical copies in pr3945/, see pr3945/SOURCES.json).
+
+On top of that closure it makes six additions:
+  new/borrow/staged_entries_applier.py, new/borrow/staged_entries_review.py,
+  new/borrow/staged3/PRE-{base,extra}.json.gz (PR3945's words),
+  new/borrow/staged3/RECORD-{base,extra}.json (our literal records).
+
+It then makes these modifications:
+  - the BORROW-WORD-43 words are replaced by ours;
+  - new/BORROW-PROVIDERS.json gets the new widths and profiles;
+  - new/rebuild_borrow.py gets one appended chain step;
+  - terminal_review.py now reads PR3945's words from staged3/PRE;
+  - verify.py gets one added review.
+
+The result is a 672-file closure. The inherited admission engine gets exactly PR3945's adaptation: source-profile
+commit, manifest and file count, plus frozen-SPEC mutation counts. Both native providers run fresh. The complete
+admission then runs on owner/FILL.json.gz, covering owners, parent lift, rebind, discovery (bind, emit, audit, invoice,
+assembly, admission, bit, independent), outer ledger and independent outer check, and release.
+
+Memory: the discovery audit (audit_allcold with mutation controls) needs about 6 GB per shard, and --jobs sets the
+shard count. The recorded run used --jobs 1 on an 8 GB Linux host (Python 3.12, numpy, scipy, sympy 1.14.0,
+mpmath 1.3.0). Runs on 6 GB, and with 4 shards on 8 GB, were killed by the memory limit during audit. That is an
+environment limit, not a check failure.
+
+authenticate.py checks the retained evidence in evidence/ against the package files with the standard library only.
+
+The mathematical claim remains conditional on the inherited uniform/all-size, source/hosting,
+precision/tape/recovery, analytic and BIT obligations. No formal kernel or independent human review is claimed.

+"""Complete native/global/outer replay for the staged-entry derivative (helpers 608, 609, 600) of PR3945's words.
+

+generator on top: literal records from PR3945's NEW words to ours, a generalized PR3734-style applier, an independent
+review with rejection controls, the rebuild-chain step, the provider registry, and our literal T360 owner fill.
+The inherited admission engine runs with only the source-profile/file-count and frozen-SPEC count adaptations
+that PR3945 already made.  Requires Python 3.12, numpy, scipy, sympy==1.14.0, mpmath==1.3.0.
+Prepared by Rohan Arun with Anthropic Claude assistance; structure and engine adaptation follow Dugongue's PR3945
+(OpenAI Codex assisted).  Apache-2.0.
+"""

+from fractions import Fraction as Q
+import argparse, gzip, hashlib, json, os, shutil, subprocess, sys, tarfile, urllib.request
+sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
+
+HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+PACKAGE = HERE.parent
+PR3945 = HERE / 'pr3945'                     # byte-identical copies of PR3945 admission inputs (see pr3945/SOURCES.json)
+HEAD = 'fa041037a3374eaa08feeca0b26a5d6893194147'
+ARCHIVE_URL = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/' + HEAD + '/research/staged544-producer-return/REPLAY-INPUTS.tar.gz'

+COMMIT = 'staged-entries-608-609-600-20261019'
+
+
+def need(ok, msg):
+    if not ok: raise ValueError(msg)
+def sha(p): return hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+def read(p):
+    b = p.read_bytes(); return json.loads(gzip.decompress(b) if p.suffix == '.gz' else b)
+def write(p, x): p.write_text(json.dumps(x, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + '\n', encoding='utf8', newline='\n')
+def tree(p, exclude=()): return {f.relative_to(p).as_posix(): sha(f) for f in sorted(p.rglob('*')) if f.is_file() and f.relative_to(p).as_posix() not in exclude}
+def patch_text(path, old, new):
+    body = path.read_text(encoding='utf8'); need(body.count(old) == 1, 'literal patch preimage ' + str(path))
+    path.write_text(body.replace(old, new), encoding='utf8', newline='\n'); return [old, new]
+
+
+def reconstruct_pr3945(work, archive):
+    """Exactly PR3945 admission/full_replay.py up to its 666-file closure."""
+    pins = read(PR3945 / 'PREDECESSOR.json'); need(sha(archive) == pins['archive_sha256'], 'pinned predecessor archive digest')
+    inputs = work / 'inputs'; inputs.mkdir(); seen = set()
+    with tarfile.open(archive) as t:
+        for m in t:
+            need(m.isfile() and not Path(m.name).is_absolute() and '..' not in Path(m.name).parts and m.name not in seen and m.name in pins['files'], 'safe declared predecessor member')
+            raw = t.extractfile(m).read(); need(hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() == pins['files'][m.name], 'predecessor member digest')
+            seen.add(m.name); out = inputs / m.name; out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); out.write_bytes(raw)
+    need(seen == set(pins['files']), 'complete 756-file retained input inventory')
+    source = inputs / 'source'
+    need(sha(source / 'MANIFEST.json') == '4c4f7067b1b5404b59213f480e9d91c96ffc79b5458e2736b159f5a522ed2dc3', 'retained 660-source manifest')
+    need(tree(source, ('MANIFEST.json',)) == read(source / 'MANIFEST.json'), 'retained source file hashes')
+    borrow = source / 'new/borrow'; terminal = borrow / 'terminal'; terminal.mkdir(); registry = read(source / 'new/BORROW-PROVIDERS.json')
+    shutil.copy2(PR3945 / 'terminal_applier.py', borrow / 'terminal_applier.py'); shutil.copy2(PR3945 / 'terminal_review.py', borrow / 'terminal_review.py')
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(borrow)); import terminal_applier as T
+    for tag, pid in [('base', 'gauge44'), ('extra', 'extra')]:
+        name = 'BORROW-WORD-43' + tag + '.json.gz'; old = borrow / 'words' / name; before = read(old)
+        final = PR3945 / ('NEW-' + tag + '.json.gz'); new = read(final)
+        shutil.copy2(old, terminal / ('PRE-' + tag + '.json.gz')); old.write_bytes(final.read_bytes())
+        record = {'source_canonical_sha256': T.canonical(before), 'candidate_canonical_sha256': T.canonical(new), 'new_fields': {k: v for k, v in new.items() if before[k] != v},
+                  'source_attribution': 'PR3734 dataisfire and retained lineage; terminal derivative Dugongue/OpenAI Codex'}
+        write(terminal / ('RECORD-' + tag + '.json'), record); need(T.apply(before, record) == new, 'declared terminal generator')
+        origin = read(PR3945 / ('old-NATIVE-' + tag + '.json.gz'))['helper_origin']; need(len(origin) == 408, 'retained native helper order')
+        registry[pid] = {'widths': [len(new['helper_final'].get(str(r), [1 << i for i in range(9)])) - len(new['start_extra'].get(str(r), [])) for r in origin],
+                         'actual_paid_profile': new['report']['local_profile']}
+    write(source / 'new/BORROW-PROVIDERS.json', registry)
+    for patch in read(PR3945 / 'SOURCE-PATCHES.json'):
+        out = source / patch['path']; need(sha(out) == patch['before_sha256'], 'generator patch source hash')
+        body = out.read_text(encoding='utf8'); need(body.count(patch['old']) == 1, 'generator patch literal preimage')
+        out.write_text(body.replace(patch['old'], patch['new']), encoding='utf8', newline='\n'); need(sha(out) == patch['after_sha256'], 'generator patch output hash')
+    write(source / 'MANIFEST.json', tree(source, ('MANIFEST.json',)))
+    need(len(read(source / 'MANIFEST.json')) == 666 and sha(source / 'MANIFEST.json') == PR3945_SOURCE_MANIFEST, 'exact PR3945 666-file source closure')
+    return inputs, source, registry
+

+def add_staged(source, registry):

+    for name in ('staged_entries_applier.py', 'staged_entries_review.py'): shutil.copy2(PACKAGE / 'recipe' / name, borrow / name)
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(borrow)); import staged_entries_applier as S
+    log = []

+        word = borrow / 'words' / ('BORROW-WORD-43' + tag + '.json.gz')
+        need(word.read_bytes() == (PACKAGE / 'inputs' / ('OLD-' + tag + '.json.gz')).read_bytes(), 'PR3945 terminal word is our source word')
+        shutil.copy2(word, staged / ('PRE-' + tag + '.json.gz'))
+        shutil.copy2(PACKAGE / 'recipe' / ('RECORD-' + tag + '.json'), staged / ('RECORD-' + tag + '.json'))

+        word.write_bytes((PACKAGE / 'inputs' / ('NEW-' + tag + '.json.gz')).read_bytes())
+        origin = read(PR3945 / ('old-NATIVE-' + tag + '.json.gz'))['helper_origin']
+        registry[pid] = {'widths': [len(new['helper_final'].get(str(r), [1 << i for i in range(9)])) - len(new['start_extra'].get(str(r), [])) for r in origin],
+                         'actual_paid_profile': new['report']['local_profile']}
+    write(source / 'new/BORROW-PROVIDERS.json', registry)

+"""Independent binary-basis ledger and declared free-operator contract for the three staged entries.
+
+The basis walker (b, subset, perpendicular, transform, inverse, ledger) is PR3945's checks/independent_frames.py
+unchanged (Dugongue, OpenAI Codex assisted); the staged-entry contract and controls are new.
+Prepared by Rohan Arun with Anthropic Claude assistance. Apache-2.0.  Standard library only.
+"""
+from pathlib import Path
+from collections import Counter
+from fractions import Fraction as Q
+import json,gzip,hashlib,sys,copy
+PACKAGE=Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+
+def need(ok,why):
+    if not ok:raise ValueError(why)
+
+def b(vectors):
+    pivots={}
+    for x in vectors:
+        need(type(x) is int and 0<=x<512,'bad frame vector')
+        while x:
+            p=x.bit_length()-1
+            if p in pivots:x^=pivots[p]
+            else:pivots[p]=x;break
+    for p in sorted(pivots):
+        for q in sorted(pivots,reverse=True):
+            if q>p and (pivots[q]>>p)&1:pivots[q]^=pivots[p]
+    return tuple(pivots[p] for p in sorted(pivots,reverse=True))
+
+def subset(A,B):return b(A+B)==B
+FULL=b([1<<j for j in range(9)])
+def perpendicular(port):
+    pivot=(port&-port).bit_length()-1
+    return b([(1<<j)^((1<<pivot) if (port>>j)&1 else 0) for j in range(9) if j!=pivot])
+def transform(F,G):
+    def apply(x):
+        y=0
+        for j in range(9):
+            if (x>>j)&1:y^=G[j]
+        return y
+    return b([apply(x) for x in F])
+def inverse(G):
+    inv={}
+    for x in range(512):
+        y=0
+        for j in range(9):
+            if x>>j&1:y^=G[j]
+        need(y not in inv,'singular native matrix');inv[y]=x
+    return [inv[1<<j] for j in range(9)]
+
+def ledger(w):
+    removed=set(w['removed']);live=set(range(704))-removed
+    start={r:b([w['ports'][r]]) if r<112 else () for r in live}
+    for r,F in w['start_extra'].items():start[int(r)]=b(F)
+    end={r:(FULL if r<112 or r>=224 else perpendicular(w['ports'][r-112])) for r in live}
+    for r,F in w['helper_final'].items():end[int(r)]=b(F)
+    cur=dict(start);profile=Counter()
+    def climb(r,F):
+        F=b(F);need(subset(cur[r],F),'nonmonotone frame at '+str(r));d=len(F)-len(cur[r]);cur[r]=F
+        if d:profile[d]+=1
+    def scalar(g):
+        for r in g[1:3] if g[0]=='add' else g[1:2]:climb(r,g[-1])
+    for g in w['A']:
+        if g[0]!='warp':scalar(g);continue
+        _,r,op,U,E=g;G=w['warps'][abs(op)-1][2]
+        if op<0:G=inverse(G)
+        need(cur[r]==b(U),'A native entry');need(transform(b(U),G)==b(E),'A native map');cur[r]=b(E)
+    for t in range(112,224):need(cur[t]==b(w['target_levels'].get(str(t-112),[])),'target cut level')
+    for r,U in zip(w['centers'],w['center_frames']):
+        need(cur[r]==b(U),'centre entry');temporary=b(U)
+        served={b(w['target_levels'].get(str(g[1]-112),[])) for g in w['cut'] if g[2]==r}
+        for T in sorted(served,key=lambda F:-len(F)):
+            need(subset(T,temporary),'centre nesting');d=len(temporary)-len(T)
+            if d:profile[d]+=1
+            temporary=T
+        # The actual descent is on a private copy; live cur[r] stays U.
+    at={}
+    for record in w['warps']:at.setdefault(record[0],[]).append(record)
+    for i in range(len(w['B'])+1):
+        for _,r,G,U,E in at.get(i,[]):
+            need(cur[r]==b(U),'B native entry');need(transform(b(U),G)==b(E),'B native map');cur[r]=b(E)
+        if i<len(w['B']):scalar(w['B'][i])
+    for g in w['restore']:scalar(g)
+    for r in sorted(live):climb(r,end[r])
+    inventory=Counter(len(end[r])-len(start[r]) for r in live if r>=224)
+    need(dict(profile)=={int(r):n for r,n in w['report']['local_profile'].items()},'profile mismatch')
+    need(dict(inventory)=={int(r):n for r,n in w['report']['width_inventory'].items()},'inventory mismatch')
+    return profile,inventory
+
+PINS=json.loads((PACKAGE/'INPUTS.json').read_text(encoding='utf8'))['canonical_sha256']
+STAGED={'600':([45],[127,45]),'608':([45],[97,45]),'609':([45],[97,45])}
+DELETED=[['add',183,600,1,4],['add',202,600,-1,4],['add',175,600,1,4],['add',123,600,-1,4],
+         ['add',114,608,1,4],['add',137,608,-1,4],['add',173,608,1,4],['add',121,608,-1,4],
+         ['add',114,609,1,4],['add',137,609,1,4],['add',173,609,1,4],['add',121,609,1,4]]
+RELEASES=[['add',121,609,1,2],['add',137,608,-1,2],['add',202,600,-1,2],['add',602,600,-1,1],['add',610,608,-1,1],['add',610,609,-1,1]]
+DELETED_AT=[77,78,79,80,93,94,95,96,97,98,99,100]
+RELEASED_AT=[388,410,474,927,948,950]
+DELTA={1:6,2:2,3:5,4:-7}
+
+def read(name):
+    w=json.loads(gzip.decompress((PACKAGE/'inputs'/name).read_bytes()))
+    scientific=hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(w,sort_keys=True,separators=(',',':')).encode()).hexdigest()
+    need(scientific==PINS[name],'canonical source guard '+name)
+    return w
+
+def signature(seq):
+    return [g[:3] if g[0]=='warp' else g[:-1] for g in seq
+            if not(g[0]=='scale' and Q(g[2],g[3])==1)]
+
+def compare(old,new):
+    for field in old:
+        if field not in ('A','B','restore','cleanup','start_extra','report','warps'):
+            need(old[field]==new[field],'changed caller field '+field)
+    need(old['helper_final']==new['helper_final'] and len(new['helper_final'])==91,'returns unchanged')
+    keys=set(old['start_extra'])|set(new['start_extra'])
+    changed={r:(old['start_extra'].get(r),new['start_extra'].get(r)) for r in keys if old['start_extra'].get(r)!=new['start_extra'].get(r)}
+    need(changed=={r:(list(x),list(y)) for r,(x,y) in STAGED.items()},'staged entrance set')
+    for r,(x,y) in changed.items():
+        need(subset(b(x),b(y)) and len(b(y))==len(b(x))+1 and r not in new['helper_final'],'entrance raised by one dimension on an ordinary helper')
+    for sec in ('A','restore'):
+        need(signature(old[sec])==signature(new[sec]),'free opcode sequence '+sec)
+    so,sn=signature(old['B']),signature(new['B'])
+    need([so[i] for i in DELETED_AT]==DELETED,'declared deleted reads at their source positions')
+    need([sn[i] for i in RELEASED_AT]==RELEASES,'declared releases at their target positions')
+    need([g for i,g in enumerate(so) if i not in DELETED_AT]==[g for i,g in enumerate(sn) if i not in RELEASED_AT],'B opcode sequence differs only by declared deletions and releases')
+    need(Counter(map(json.dumps,sn))==Counter(map(json.dumps,so))-Counter(map(json.dumps,DELETED))+Counter(map(json.dumps,RELEASES)),'opcode multiset balance')
+    need([r[1:3] for r in old['warps']]==[r[1:3] for r in new['warps']],'native matrices/lenders')
+    po,io=ledger(old);pn,inn=ledger(new)
+    delta={r:pn[r]-po[r] for r in set(po)|set(pn) if pn[r]!=po[r]}
+    need(delta==DELTA and sum(r*n for r,n in delta.items())==-3,'local profile delta/rank mass')
+    need(io==Counter({5:28,6:18,7:53,8:96,9:213}),'old width inventory')
+    need(inn==Counter({5:28,6:18,7:56,8:93,9:213}),'new width inventory')
+    return {'old_profile':dict(po),'new_profile':dict(pn),'local_profile_delta':delta,'staged_entrances':sorted(changed,key=int),'deleted_reads':len(DELETED),'releases':len(RELEASES),'buffers':91}
+
+def controls(old,new):
+    outcomes=[]
+    def reject(label,callback):
+        try:callback()
+        except ValueError:outcomes.append(label);return
+        raise ValueError('mutation was accepted: '+label)
+    z=copy.deepcopy(new);z['report']['local_profile']['1']+=1
+    reject('wrong paid histogram',lambda:ledger(z))
+    z=copy.deepcopy(new);z['warps'][0][4]=[]
+    reject('wrong native exit frame',lambda:ledger(z))
+    z=copy.deepcopy(new);z['start_extra']['608']=[45]
+    reject('missing staged entrance',lambda:compare(old,z))
+    z=copy.deepcopy(new);k=next(i for i,g in enumerate(z['B']) if g[:-1]==RELEASES[0]);z['B'][k][3]+=1
+    reject('changed release coefficient',lambda:compare(old,z))
+    z=copy.deepcopy(new);g=next(g for g in z['A'] if g[0]=='add');g[3]+=1
+    reject('changed scalar operator',lambda:compare(old,z))
+    return outcomes
+
+def main():
+    results={};mutation_checks=[]
+    for provider in ('base','extra'):
+        old,new=read('OLD-'+provider+'.json.gz'),read('NEW-'+provider+'.json.gz')
+        results[provider]=compare(old,new)
+        if '--controls' in sys.argv:mutation_checks += [provider+': '+x for x in controls(old,new)]
+    print(json.dumps({'status':'PASS_INDEPENDENT_BINARY_BASIS_LEDGER','canonical_source_sha256':PINS,'providers':results,'rejected_controls':mutation_checks,'scope':'Independent local binary frames, exact histogram/inventory and declared staged-entry operator contract; native phases, dirty semantics and literal owner/outer assembly checked separately.'},sort_keys=True))
+
+if __name__=='__main__':main()

+    need(__debug__, 'assertions must remain enabled')

+    parser.add_argument('work', type=Path)
+    parser.add_argument('--engine', choices=('reference', 'sparse'), default='sparse')
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    started = time.monotonic()
+    blobs = source_bytes(HERE / 'vendor')
+    original = args.word.resolve()
+    need(original.is_file(), 'input word missing')
+    body = original.read_bytes()
+    work = args.work.resolve()
+    need(not work.exists(), 'fresh work directory required')
+    work.mkdir(parents=True)
+    vendor = work / 'source'
+    for name, contents in blobs.items():
+        target = vendor / name
+        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

+    env.pop('PYTHONOPTIMIZE', None)
+    commands = []
+    def run(name, command, cwd):
+        before = time.monotonic()
+        with (work / (name + '.log')).open('w') as log:
+            result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=cwd, env=env, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+                                    stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
+        entry = {'step': name, 'exit_code': result.returncode,
+                 'seconds': time.monotonic()-before, 'command': command}
+        commands.append(entry)
+        (work / 'COMMANDS.json').write_text(json.dumps(commands, indent=2)+'\n')
+        need(result.returncode == 0, 'stage failed: '+name+'; see '+str(work/(name+'.log')))

+    if args.engine == 'reference':
+        run('reference-driver', [sys.executable, '-I', '-B', str(vendor/'native/new/run_native_borrow.py'), str(word), str(output)], native)
+        steps = json.loads((output/'STEPS.json').read_text())
+    else:
+        output.mkdir()
+        local = output/'local'
+        plan = [

+            ('phases', [('bw_phases.py', [local]), ('bw_check_recipes.py', [local])]),

+            for script, arguments in scripts:

+                else:
+                    command = [sys.executable, '-I', '-B', str(native/script)]

+#!/usr/bin/env python3

+from pathlib import Path

+import sys
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
+from common import need, source_bytes
+
+def module(name, path):
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
+    result = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    sys.modules[name] = result
+    spec.loader.exec_module(result)
+    return result
+
+def main():
+    need(__debug__, 'assertions must remain enabled')
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument('--vendor', type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument('--script', choices=('bw_adapters.py', 'bw_phases.py'), required=True)

+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    vendor = args.vendor.resolve()
+    source_bytes(vendor)
+    native = vendor / 'native/new/code/borrow'
+    algebra = module('clifford_exact', native / 'vendor/clifford/clifford_exact.py')

+
+if __name__ == '__main__':

+# Exact support updates
+
+This argument applies to the valid gates from the pinned `clifford_exact.py`.
+The input is a basis index `0 <= basis < 2^n`. Each state has Gaussian integer
+numerators and a common denominator `2^den`. A missing dictionary key has
+numerator zero. The output contains all `2^n` numerators, including zeros.
+
+## Induction over the circuit
+
+The initial dictionary has the one entry `basis -> (1, 0)`. It is the same
+state as the retained dense evaluator.
+
+For `P`, the validated binary matrix is invertible. Its index map is a
+permutation. Thus no two nonzero entries collide, and omitted zero entries
+contribute no value. For `X`, translation by XOR is also a permutation.
+
+For `D` and `phase`, each amplitude is multiplied by a power of `i`. The
+four rotations of `(a, b)` are `(a, b)`, `(-b, a)`, `(-a, -b)`, and `(b, -a)`.
+Zero remains zero. The `D` phases and `P` index maps use the unchanged PR662
+tables. Those tables depend on the dimension and all gate coefficients.
+They do not depend on a state or on a previous check result. The source pins
+retain their exact formulas and bounded caches.
+
+For `C`, put `y = x xor q` and let `s` be the sign. If the numerators at
+`x` and `y` are `(a, b)` and `(c, d)`, the new numerators are
+
+```text
+x: (a - s*b + c + s*d, b + s*a + d - s*c)
+y: (c - s*d + a + s*b, d + s*c + b - s*a).
+```
+
+The denominator exponent increases by one. These are the two rows of the
+retained dense update. XOR partitions the index set into pairs when `q != 0`.
+The loop visits a pair once if either entry is nonzero. If both entries are
+present, it skips the larger index. If only one entry is present, its partner
+has value zero. A pair with two zero entries contributes two zeros and need
+not be visited. Exact cancellation removes a zero output entry. When `q = 0`,
+both formulas give `(2*a, 2*b)` at the same index; the update is the identity
+after division by two.
+
+The common-factor test after `C` gives the same answer on the dictionary as
+on the dense vector: omitted entries are zero and are divisible by two.
+The other gates only permute entries or rotate their Gaussian coordinates.
+They cannot change the common power of two. Thus those gates need no further
+normalization. This proves equality of both the complete vector and `den`
+after every gate. It also covers circuits whose support shrinks after a
+`C` gate. A valid Clifford circuit cannot map a nonzero input to the zero
+state, because each gate is invertible.
+
+## The compiler checks
+
+`lowering.py` retains the algebra and checks of the pinned lowering routine.
+It passes a state evaluator through ordinary function arguments. It changes
+no retained module, method or global value. The reference mode calls the
+original lowering routine. The dense and sparse modes use the same explicit
+lowering code with their respective evaluators.
+
+Every tableau equality, off-support zero check, denominator check, and global
+phase check remains. The final comparison still checks the complete compiled
+state against the complete input state. No phase is inferred from a tableau.
+
+`run.py` retains the frame-span, frame-rank, edge-rank and endpoint-rank checks
+of `phases_full.py`. It visits every frame, every directed edge including
+center transitions, and every source and target adapter. Its public entry
+point rejects optimized Python before it loads the retained assertion-based
+algebra. It also rejects source drift and an existing output directory.
+
+## Work and storage
+
+Let `s` be the current number of nonzero amplitudes and `N = 2^n`. A state
+update now visits `s` entries, or at most `s` XOR pairs, in place of all `N`
+entries. Dictionary operations have their usual expected constant lookup
+cost. Integer arithmetic remains exact. A first use of a PR662 gate table
+still takes `O(N)` work, and the final full output also takes `O(N)` work.
+Each of the two retained table caches has at most 64 entries.
+
+This is a support-sensitive improvement. It is not a polynomial-size
+stabilizer representation: the support can be all `N` indices. The benchmark
+measures the complete selected dimension-nine phase command, including table
+construction, source admission, parsing, lowering, checks and output writing.
+It makes no claim about multiplication runtime or the full cold replay.

+"""Evaluate exact Clifford states on their nonzero support.
+
+Gate tables are from Charles Bethin's PR662. The support update is new.
+Prepared for Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.
+Apache-2.0.
+"""
+
+
+def zero_state(op, tables, basis=0):
+    """Return every Gaussian numerator and the power-of-two denominator."""
+    size = 1 << op.n
+    if not 0 <= basis < size:
+        raise IndexError(basis)
+    state = {basis: (1, 0)}
+    den = 0
+    for gate in op.circuit:
+        kind = gate[0]
+        if kind == 'P':
+            mapping = tables.permutation_table(op.n, tuple(gate[1]))
+            state = {mapping[x]: value for x, value in state.items()}
+        elif kind == 'X':
+            state = {x ^ gate[1]: value for x, value in state.items()}
+        elif kind in ('D', 'phase'):
+            phases = (tables.phase_table(op.n, tuple(gate[1]), tuple(gate[2]))
+                      if kind == 'D' else None)
+            out = {}
+            for x, (a, b) in state.items():
+                phase = phases[x] if phases is not None else gate[1] % 4
+                if phase == 0:
+                    out[x] = (a, b)
+                elif phase == 1:
+                    out[x] = (-b, a)
+                elif phase == 2:
+                    out[x] = (-a, -b)
+                else:
+                    out[x] = (b, -a)
+            state = out
+        elif kind == 'C':
+            q, sign = gate[1:]
+            out = {}
+            for x, (a, b) in state.items():
+                y = x ^ q
+                if y < x and y in state:
+                    continue
+                c, d = state.get(y, (0, 0))
+                first = (a - sign*b + c + sign*d,
+                         b + sign*a + d - sign*c)
+                second = (c - sign*d + a + sign*b,
+                          d + sign*c + b - sign*a)
+                if first != (0, 0):
+                    out[x] = first
+                if second != (0, 0):
+                    out[y] = second
+            state = out
+            den += 1
+            while den and all((a & 1) == (b & 1) == 0
+                              for a, b in state.values()):
+                state = {x: (a // 2, b // 2) for x, (a, b) in state.items()}
+                den -= 1
+        else:
+            raise AssertionError(gate)
+    vec = [(0, 0)] * size
+    for x, value in state.items():
+        vec[x] = value
+    return vec, den

+"""Exact Gaussian-dyadic state evaluation with bounded, state-free gate tables.
+
+Charles Bethin, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0.
+The gate semantics and normalization follow the pinned clifford_exact.py.
+"""
+from functools import lru_cache
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=64)
+def permutation_table(n, rows):
+    """Compute Gx from G(x xor lowbit(x)) xor G(lowbit(x))."""
+    columns = [sum(((row >> j) & 1) << i for i, row in enumerate(rows))
+               for j in range(n)]
+    table = [0] * (1 << n)
+    for x in range(1, len(table)):
+        bit = x & -x
+        table[x] = table[x ^ bit] ^ columns[bit.bit_length() - 1]
+    return tuple(table)
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=64)
+def phase_table(n, rows, linear):
+    """Remove the lowest bit; all remaining quadratic partners have larger indices."""
+    table = [0] * (1 << n)
+    for x in range(1, len(table)):
+        bit = x & -x
+        i, rest = bit.bit_length() - 1, x ^ bit
+        table[x] = (table[rest] + linear[i] +
+                    2 * ((rows[i] & rest).bit_count() & 1)) % 4
+    return tuple(table)
+
+
+def clear_caches():
+    permutation_table.cache_clear()
+    phase_table.cache_clear()
+
+
+def zero_state(self, basis=0):
+    """Drop-in evaluator for valid pinned Op circuits; return the full exact state."""
+    size = 1 << self.n
+    vec = [(0, 0)] * size
+    vec[basis] = (1, 0)
+    den = 0
+    for gate in self.circuit:
+        kind = gate[0]
+        if kind == 'P':
+            mapping = permutation_table(self.n, tuple(gate[1]))
+            out = [(0, 0)] * size
+            for x, value in enumerate(vec):
+                out[mapping[x]] = value
+            vec = out
+        elif kind == 'X':
+            vec = [vec[x ^ gate[1]] for x in range(size)]
+        elif kind in ('D', 'phase'):
+            phases = (phase_table(self.n, tuple(gate[1]), tuple(gate[2]))
+                      if kind == 'D' else [gate[1] % 4] * size)
+            out = []
+            for (a, b), phase in zip(vec, phases):
+                if phase == 0:
+                    out.append((a, b))
+                elif phase == 1:
+                    out.append((-b, a))
+                elif phase == 2:
+                    out.append((-a, -b))
+                else:
+                    out.append((b, -a))
+            vec = out
+        elif kind == 'C':
+            q, sign = gate[1:]
+            out = []
+            for x, (a, b) in enumerate(vec):
+                c, d = vec[x ^ q]
+                out.append((a - sign*b + c + sign*d,
+                            b + sign*a + d - sign*c))
+            vec = out
+            den += 1
+        else:
+            raise AssertionError(gate)
+        while den and all((a & 1) == (b & 1) == 0 for a, b in vec):
+            vec = [(a // 2, b // 2) for a, b in vec]
+            den -= 1
+    return vec, den

+"""Transport an explicit BORROW-WORD to the native canonical frame-id form, with warps, and replay it exactly.
+
+Anticipatory dirty borrowing is the construction of PR2226 (Cinna Davis, @1337isnot1337, with OpenAI Codex
+assistance; Apache-2.0): a retiring helper's register is lent to a later helper through a monomial Clifford
+logical reference change K_G ("warp"), the retired field's value being replaced by K_G z. The explicit
+chronological BORROW-WORD (canonical coordinates, literal frames, warps, cold restoration, inverse cleanup
+with private zero buffers) is the builder output of the borrowing work (P1/P2).  This script is the
+transport stage of the native chain (the analogue of hpe_audit_and_transport.py): it never trusts the builder.
+It replays the program in the free operator algebra generated by the warps over every arbitrary input,
+in BOTH orientations (forward and inverse-transpose), checks every frame chain and the paid profile, compacts
+the helper registers to R' = R - k, and writes the native CANONICAL-WORD.
+
+usage: bw_transport.py BORROW-WORD.json[.gz] OUT_DIR
+"""
+if not __debug__:
+    raise RuntimeError('assertions must remain enabled')   # every check of this stage is an assert
+import argparse
+import copy
+import gzip
+import hashlib
+import json
+import sys
+import time
+from collections import Counter
+from fractions import Fraction as Q
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def read(path):
+    data = path.read_bytes()
+    return json.loads(gzip.decompress(data) if path.suffix == '.gz' else data)
+
+
+def basis(vs):
+    pivots = {}
+    for x in vs:
+        for k in sorted(pivots, reverse=True):
+            if x >> k & 1:
+                x ^= pivots[k]
+        if x:
+            k = x.bit_length() - 1
+            for j in pivots:
+                if pivots[j] >> k & 1:
+                    pivots[j] ^= x
+            pivots[k] = x
+    return tuple(pivots[k] for k in sorted(pivots, reverse=True))
+
+
+def span(b):
+    s = {0}
+    for x in b:
+        s |= {t ^ x for t in s}
+    return frozenset(s)
+
+
+def rank_of(vs):
+    return len(basis(vs))
+
+
+def solve_G(cols, h):
+    """G given as images of e_i; returns (invertible?, image-of-subspace function)."""
+    def lin(x):
+        out = 0
+        for i, c in enumerate(cols):
+            if x >> i & 1:
+                out ^= c
+        return out
+    return lin, rank_of(cols) == h
+
+
+# ---- free operator algebra over the warps ------------------------------------------------------------------
+def add_row(dst, src, c):
+    for key, value in list(src.items()):
+        z = dst.get(key, Q(0)) + c * value
+        if z:
+            dst[key] = z
+        elif key in dst:
+            del dst[key]
+
+
+def warp_row(row, op):
+    out = {}
+    for (var, word), value in row.items():
+        word = word[1:] if word and word[0] == -op else (op,) + word
+        out[var, word] = value
+    return out
+
+
+def is_dyadic(q):
+    return q.denominator & (q.denominator - 1) == 0
+
+
+def gate_regs(e):
+    if e[0] == 'add':
+        return [e[1], e[2]]
+    if e[0] == 'scale':
+        return [e[1]]
+    raise AssertionError(e[0])
+
+
+def dual(e):
+    e = list(e)
+    if e[0] == 'add':
+        e[1], e[2] = e[2], e[1]
+        e[3] = -e[3]
+    elif e[0] == 'scale':
+        e[2], e[3] = e[3], e[2]
+    return e
+
+
+def apply_gate(e, rows, back):
+    if back:
+        e = dual(e)
+    if e[0] == 'scale':
+        q = Q(e[2], e[3])
+        assert q
+        rows[e[1]] = {j: q * x for j, x in rows[e[1]].items()}
+    else:
+        assert e[1] != e[2]
+        add_row(rows[e[1]], rows[e[2]], Q(e[3], e[4]))
+
+
+def run(word_path, out):
+    t0 = time.monotonic()
+    word = read(word_path)

+"""Native chain for a BORROW-WORD (anticipatory dirty borrowing, PR2226): transport -> emit -> independent replay -> wrappers -> phases (+ independent warp-recipe recheck).
+Same step layout and STEPS.json as the lineage replay_native.py; usage: run_native_borrow.py BORROW-WORD.json[.gz] WORK_DIR  (WORK_DIR must not exist)."""
+import json,os,subprocess,sys,time
+from pathlib import Path
+HERE=Path(__file__).resolve().parent/'code/borrow'
+word=Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve();work=Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve();work.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=False);local=work/'local'
+env=dict(os.environ,PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE='1',PYTHONUTF8='1',PYTHONINTMAXSTRDIGITS='0');env.pop('PYTHONOPTIMIZE',None)
+flags=(0x00000040|0x08000000) if os.name=='nt' and os.environ.get('BW_IDLE','1')=='1' else 0   # windowless, IDLE priority
+steps=[]
+for label,script,args in [('native',HERE/'bw_transport.py',[word,local]),('ledgers',HERE/'bw_emit.py',[local]),
+        ('local-replay',HERE/'bw_audit_local.py',[local]),
+        ('wrappers',HERE/'bw_adapters.py',[local/'CANONICAL-WORD.json.gz',local/'RESIDUAL-ADAPTERS.json',local/'WRAPPER-CHECKS.json']),
+        ('phases',[HERE/'bw_phases.py',HERE/'bw_check_recipes.py'],[local])]:   # phases = exact lowering, then the independent warp-recipe recheck
+    t=time.monotonic();log=b''
+    for script in (script if isinstance(script,list) else [script]):
+        p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-B',str(script),*map(str,args)],stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,cwd=HERE,env=env,creationflags=flags)
+        log+=p.stdout
+        if p.returncode:break
+    (work/(label+'.log')).write_bytes(log)

+    assert p.returncode==0,(label,log.decode(errors='replace')[-4000:])
+    print('PASS',label,round(steps[-1]['seconds'],1),flush=True)

+"""Build the literal staged-entry RECORD from PR3945's NEW word and the staged word (provenance tool)."""
+import sys, json, gzip, difflib
+sys.path.insert(0, '/home/claude/pkg'); sys.path.insert(0, '/home/claude/adm/prep3945/inputs/source/new/borrow')
+import staged_entries_applier as S
+
+def slices(old, new):
+    sm = difflib.SequenceMatcher(a=[json.dumps(g) for g in old], b=[json.dumps(g) for g in new], autojunk=False)
+    return [{'slice': [i1, i2], 'old': old[i1:i2], 'new': new[j1:j2]} for op, i1, i2, j1, j2 in sm.get_opcodes() if op != 'equal']
+
+def record(parent, w, entries):
+    r = {'schema': 'staged-entries-literal-v1', 'source_canonical_sha256': S.canonical(parent), 'target_canonical_sha256': S.canonical(w),
+         'sections': {sec: slices(parent[sec], w[sec]) for sec in ('A', 'B', 'restore') if parent[sec] != w[sec]},
+         'entrances': [{'helper': h, 'old': parent['start_extra'][h], 'new': w['start_extra'][h]} for h in sorted(w['start_extra'], key=int) if parent['start_extra'].get(h) != w['start_extra'][h]],
+         'warps': w['warps'], 'report': {k: w['report'][k] for k in ('local_profile', 'width_inventory')}, 'entries': entries}
+    assert S.apply(parent, r) == w
+    return r
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    old, new, out = sys.argv[1:4]
+    entries = json.loads(open(sys.argv[4]).read())
+    r = record(json.load(gzip.open(old)), json.load(gzip.open(new)), entries)
+    open(out, 'w').write(json.dumps(r, indent=1, sort_keys=True) + '\n')
+    print('record', out, {s: len(v) for s, v in r['sections'].items()}, 'entrances', [(e['helper'], e['old'], e['new']) for e in r['entrances']])

+"""Literal pinned staged-entry edits on PR3945's terminal-width5 words; no optimizer is needed to replay them.
+
+Generalizes dataisfire's PR3734 stage544_applier (helper 544) to the three staged helpers 608, 609 and 600:
+ordered literal slice edits of the scalar sections, explicit entrance (start_extra) raises with preimages,
+native warps whose identities and maps are preserved, the declared report, and the derived cleanup.
+Prepared by Rohan Arun with Anthropic Claude assistance. Apache-2.0.
+"""
+import copy, hashlib, json
+
+
+def canonical(w): return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(w, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')).encode()).hexdigest()
+def need(ok, why):
+    if not ok: raise ValueError(why)
+
+
+def apply(parent, record):
+    need(record.get('schema') == 'staged-entries-literal-v1', 'record schema')
+    need(canonical(parent) == record['source_canonical_sha256'], 'source canonical digest')
+    w = copy.deepcopy(parent)
+    for sec, edits in record['sections'].items():
+        need(sec in ('A', 'B', 'restore'), 'scalar section')
+        old = parent[sec]; out = []; cursor = 0
+        for edit in edits:
+            a, b = edit['slice']; need(cursor <= a <= b <= len(old), 'ordered slice')
+            need(old[a:b] == edit['old'], 'literal scalar preimage')
+            out += copy.deepcopy(old[cursor:a]) + copy.deepcopy(edit['new']); cursor = b
+        w[sec] = out + copy.deepcopy(old[cursor:])
+    seen = set()
+    for e in record['entrances']:
+        h = e['helper']; need(h not in seen and h not in parent['helper_final'], 'ordinary staged helper')
+        need(parent['start_extra'].get(h) == e['old'], 'entrance preimage')
+        need(len(e['new']) == len(e['old']) + 1, 'entrance raised by exactly one dimension')
+        seen.add(h); w['start_extra'][h] = copy.deepcopy(e['new'])
+    need(len(parent['warps']) == len(record['warps']), 'warp inventory')
+    need(all(a[1:3] == b[1:3] for a, b in zip(parent['warps'], record['warps'])), 'native identities and maps preserved')
+    w['warps'] = copy.deepcopy(record['warps']); w['report'].update(copy.deepcopy(record['report']))
+    from staged_pair import cleanup
+    w['cleanup'] = cleanup(w)
+    need(set(k for k in parent if parent[k] != w[k]) <= {'A', 'B', 'restore', 'start_extra', 'warps', 'report', 'cleanup'}, 'changed field contract')
+    need(canonical(w) == record['target_canonical_sha256'], 'target canonical digest')
+    return w

+"""Independent exact semantics and binary-frame bill for the BORROW-WORD format.
+
+Standard library only. Nothing is imported from the audited authors' code
+(PR3133/PR3605 producers, cleanup generator, evaluator or frame solver); the word
+format and its semantic contract were read from those pinned sources and are
+credited there.  The frame-bill and free-word structure (point-set spans, warp
+frame and lifted-frame checks, target levels keyed by register, dual symbol
+naming) re-implements, without importing, Arham Tahir's
+research/coupled-carrier-independent-audit/verify.py (Apache-2.0) and shares its
+reading of the contract, so this module is not independent of that audit.
+
+Sagar Thakrar (thakrarsagar), with substantial AI assistance from Claude
+(Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5). Apache-2.0.
+"""
+from collections import Counter
+from fractions import Fraction as Q
+
+V, N, H = 112, 704, 9          # sources 0..111, targets 112..223, helpers 224..703
+DUAL = 10 ** 6                  # offset naming the independent dual symbols D_k = K_k^(-T)
+
+
+class AuditFailure(Exception):
+    """Explicit failure; never disabled by python -O."""
+
+
+def need(ok, *why):
+    if not ok:
+        raise AuditFailure(' '.join(map(str, why)))
+
+
+def is_target(r):
+    return V <= r < 2 * V
+
+
+def touched(g):
+    return g[1:3] if g[0] == 'add' else g[1:2]
+
+
+# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Binary frames: a subspace of F_2^9 is stored as a 512-bit point-set mask
+# (bit x set iff x lies in the subspace).  Containment is mask inclusion.
+# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+_SPAN = {}
+
+
+def span(vectors):
+    key = tuple(vectors)
+    mask = _SPAN.get(key)
+    if mask is None:
+        points = {0}
+        for u in key:
+            need(type(u) is int and 0 <= u < 512, 'frame vector out of range', u)
+            if u not in points:
+                points |= {p ^ u for p in points}
+        mask = sum(1 << p for p in points)
+        _SPAN[key] = mask
+    return mask
+
+
+def points(mask):
+    return [x for x in range(512) if mask >> x & 1]
+
+
+def dim(mask):
+    size = bin(mask).count('1')
+    need(size and size & (size - 1) == 0, 'not a subspace point set')
+    return size.bit_length() - 1
+
+
+FULL = (1 << 512) - 1
+ZERO = 1
+
+
+def hyperplane(port):
+    return sum(1 << x for x in range(512) if bin(x & port).count('1') % 2 == 0)
+
+
+def warp_images(columns):
+    """Images of all 512 vectors under the F_2-linear map with columns G e_i."""
+    need(len(columns) == H and all(type(c) is int and 0 <= c < 512 for c in columns), 'warp columns')
+    images = [0] * 512
+    for x in range(1, 512):
+        low = x & -x
+        images[x] = images[x ^ low] ^ columns[low.bit_length() - 1]
+    need(len(set(images)) == 512, 'singular warp')
+    return images
+
+
+def image_mask(images, mask):
+    return sum(1 << images[x] for x in points(mask))
+
+
+def lagrangian_action_ok(images, U, E):
+    """K_G(x,z)=(Gx, Gx+G^{-T}(x+z)) is symplectic and maps L_U to L_E, L_0 and L_FULL to themselves.
+
+    L_U={(x,x+p): x in U, p in U^perp}.  This is the binary frame action only; it
+    is not a Clifford phase or Gaussian-product certificate.  For invertible G with
+    G(U)=E it is implied by the frame-map check (<G^-T p, Gu> = <p, u>), so it is a
+    consistency check of the implementation, not extra evidence.
+    """
+    inverse = [0] * 512
+    for x, y in enumerate(images):
+        inverse[y] = x
+    # G^{-T} z: bit j of the result is <G^{-1} e_j, z>.
+    git = lambda z: sum((bin(inverse[1 << j] & z).count('1') & 1) << j for j in range(H))
+    lift = lambda x, z: (images[x], images[x] ^ git(x ^ z))
+    pair = lambda a, b: (bin(a[0] & b[1]).count('1') + bin(a[1] & b[0]).count('1')) & 1
+    basis = [(1 << i, 0) for i in range(H)] + [(0, 1 << i) for i in range(H)]
+    lifted = [lift(*b) for b in basis]
+    if any(pair(lifted[i], lifted[j]) != pair(basis[i], basis[j]) for i in range(18) for j in range(i + 1, 18)):
+        return False
+
+    def frame(mask):
+        us = points(mask)
+        perp = [p for p in range(512) if all(bin(p & u).count('1') % 2 == 0 for u in us)]
+        return {(u, u ^ p) for u in us for p in perp}
+    return all({lift(*pt) for pt in frame(a)} == frame(b) for a, b in ((ZERO, ZERO), (FULL, FULL), (U, E)))
+
+
+# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Chronological binary-frame bill (BORROW-WORD contract)
+# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+def frame_bill(w, lagrangian=False):
+    rep = w['report']
+    need((rep['v'], 2 * rep['v'] + rep['R'], rep['h']) == (V, N, H), 'word geometry')
+    removed = set(w['removed'])
+    need(len(removed) == len(w['removed']) and all(2 * V <= r < N for r in removed), 'removed helpers')
+    live = [r for r in range(N) if r not in removed]
+    liveset = set(live)
+    B, warps = w['B'], w['warps']
+    for k, (pos, lender, cols, U, E) in enumerate(warps, 1):
+        need(0 <= pos <= len(B), 'warp position', k)
+        need(lender in liveset and not is_target(lender), 'warp lender', k)
+        images = warp_images(cols)
+        su, se = span(U), span(E)
+        need(dim(su) == len(U) == len(E) == dim(se), 'warp frame bases', k)
+        need(image_mask(images, su) == se, 'warp does not map its frame', k)
+        if lagrangian:
+            need(lagrangian_action_ok(images, su, se), 'lifted frame action', k)
+    for name in ('A', 'B', 'restore'):

+    else:

+"""Deterministic declared staged entrance edit; Python standard library only.
+
+The record contains every scalar edit and solved-frame preimage. This applier
+does not search or optimize frames and derives inverse cleanup literally.
+"""
+import copy,gzip,hashlib,json,sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+def canonical(w):
+    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(w,sort_keys=True,separators=(',',':')).encode()).hexdigest()
+
+def require(ok,why):
+    if not ok:raise ValueError(why)
+
+def cleanup(w):
+    n=2*w['report']['v']+w['report']['R'];rest=set(map(int,w['helper_final']))
+    full=[256,128,64,32,16,8,4,2,1];fw=list(w['A'][w['prelude_events']:]);by={}
+    for op,rec in enumerate(w['warps'],1):by.setdefault(rec[0],[]).append(['warp',rec[1],op])
+    for i in range(len(w['B'])+1):
+        fw+=by.get(i,[])
+        if i<len(w['B']):fw.append(w['B'][i])
+    fw+=w['restore'];out=[]
+    buf=lambda r:r+n if r in rest else r
+    for g in reversed(fw):
+        if g[0]=='warp':out.append(['warp',buf(g[1]),-g[2],list(full)])
+        elif 112<=g[1]<224:continue
+        elif g[0]=='add':out.append(['add',buf(g[1]),buf(g[2]),-g[3],g[4],list(full)])
+        else:
+            require(g[0]=='scale','unknown cleanup primitive')
+            out.append(['scale',buf(g[1]),g[3],g[2],list(full)])
+    return out
+
+def apply(parent,record):
+    require(record['schema']=='staged-entering-pair-v1','record schema')
+    require(canonical(parent)==record['source_canonical_sha256'],'source word digest')
+    require(set(record['pivots'])=={644,660},'exact two pivots')
+    x=copy.deepcopy(parent)
+    deleted={r['index']:r['old'] for r in record['B_deleted']}
+    require(set(deleted)==set(range(184,188))|set(range(216,220)),'exact deleted indices')
+    require(all(parent['B'][i]==g for i,g in deleted.items()),'deleted scalar preimages')
+    added={r['before']:r['gates'] for r in record['B_inserted']}
+    require(set(added)=={599,647},'exact release cuts')
+    require([[g[:-1] for g in added[i]] for i in (599,647)]==[
+        [['add',640,644,2,1],['add',496,644,-2,1]],
+        [['add',656,660,-1,1],['add',520,660,-2,1]]],'exact release scalars')
+    bframes={r['parent_index']:r for r in record['B_frame_edits']};nb=[];positions={}
+    for i in range(len(parent['B'])+1):
+        positions[i]=len(nb);nb+=copy.deepcopy(added.get(i,[]))
+        if i==len(parent['B']) or i in deleted:continue
+        g=copy.deepcopy(parent['B'][i])
+        if i in bframes:
+            r=bframes[i];require(g[-1]==r['old'],'B frame preimage')
+            g[-1]=copy.deepcopy(r['new'])
+        nb.append(g)
+    require(set(bframes)<=set(range(len(parent['B'])))-set(deleted),'B frame index')
+    x['B']=nb
+    for rec in x['warps']:rec[0]=positions[rec[0]]
+    for sec in ('A','restore'):
+        seen=set()
+        for r in record[sec+'_frame_edits']:
+            i=r['index'];require(i not in seen,'duplicate frame edit');seen.add(i)
+            require(x[sec][i][-1]==r['old'] and x[sec][i][0]!='warp',sec+' frame preimage')
+            x[sec][i][-1]=copy.deepcopy(r['new'])
+    require(record['start_frames']=={'644':{'old':[30],'new':[429,30]},'660':{'old':[30],'new':[429,30]}},'exact paired entrances')
+    for h,r in record['start_frames'].items():
+        require(x['start_extra'][h]==r['old'] and h not in x['helper_final'],'ordinary FULL helper entrance')
+        x['start_extra'][h]=list(r['new'])
+    require(set(record['report'])=={'local_profile','width_inventory'},'only derived report fields')
+    x['report'].update(copy.deepcopy(record['report']))
+    x['cleanup']=cleanup(x)
+    require(canonical(x)==record['target_canonical_sha256'],'reconstructed target digest')
+    return x
+
+def main():
+    p,r,o=map(Path,sys.argv[1:]);raw=p.read_bytes();recraw=r.read_bytes()
+    parent=json.loads(gzip.decompress(raw) if p.suffix=='.gz' else raw)
+    record=json.loads(gzip.decompress(recraw) if r.suffix=='.gz' else recraw)
+    require(hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()==record['source_compressed_sha256'],'source compressed digest')
+    out=bytearray(gzip.compress(json.dumps(apply(parent,record),separators=(',',':')).encode(),compresslevel=9,mtime=0))
+    # CPython versions differ in the non-semantic gzip OS header byte.
+    # The frozen word uses the recorded byte; the DEFLATE payload is retained.
+    out[9]=record['gzip_os_byte'];out=bytes(out)
+    require(hashlib.sha256(out).hexdigest()==record['target_compressed_sha256'],'literal target byte digest')
+    o.write_bytes(out);print('PASS_DETERMINISTIC_STAGED_ENTRANCE_PAIR',record['provider'])
+
+if __name__=='__main__':main()

+"""Fresh local reconstruction and exact semantics of the staged-entry words; authenticate the fresh native receipts.
+
+From PR3945's terminal-width5 words (inputs/OLD-*), the literal records in recipe/ reconstruct the staged-entry words
+(inputs/NEW-*) with no search or solver.  Each word must pass PR3734/PR3945 hygiene, the Lagrangian frame bill equal
+to its declared report, and arbitrary-dirty forward, dual and cleanup-boundary semantics (audit_core of Sagar Thakrar
+PR3687/3693, as used by PR3945's apply_terminal.exact_semantics).  Native receipts are authenticated; the native
+phases themselves are a separate fresh-run command (native/run_native.py).
+Prepared by Rohan Arun with Anthropic Claude assistance. Apache-2.0.
+"""
+import gzip, hashlib, json, sys
+from fractions import Fraction as Q
+from pathlib import Path
+HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE / 'vendor')); sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE / 'recipe'))
+import audit_core as C
+import staged_entries_applier as S
+
+
+def need(ok, why):
+    if not ok: raise ValueError(why)
+def read(p):
+    b = p.read_bytes(); return json.loads(gzip.decompress(b) if p.suffix == '.gz' else b)
+
+
+def exact_semantics(w):
+    need(C.endpoint_defects(w, C.forward_rows(w, symbolic_buffers=True)) == ([], [], [], True), 'arbitrary-dirty forward')
+    need(C.endpoint_defects(w, C.forward_rows(w, dual=True, symbolic_buffers=True), dual=True) == ([], [], [], True), 'arbitrary-dirty dual')
+    need(not C.boundary_defects(w, C.transpose(C.reverse_columns(w, upto_cleanup=True))), 'cleanup boundary')
+
+
+def load(root=HERE):
+    pins = read(root / 'INPUTS.json')
+    for name, digest in pins['gzip_sha256'].items(): need(hashlib.sha256((root / 'inputs' / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest() == digest, 'input hash: ' + name)
+    return [(tag, read(root / 'inputs' / f'OLD-{tag}.json.gz'), read(root / 'recipe' / f'RECORD-{tag}.json'), read(root / 'inputs' / f'NEW-{tag}.json.gz')) for tag in ('base', 'extra')]

+    declared = read(HERE / 'RESULT.json')
+    need({int(k): v for k, v in declared['full_profile'].items()} == FULL_PROFILE, 'result profile')
+    need(Q(declared['root_lower']) == LOWER and Q(declared['root_upper']) == UPPER, 'result root interval')
+    need(Q(declared['conditional_kappa']) == OUTER_LOWER, 'result conditional endpoint')
+    closure = {p.relative_to(HERE / 'native/vendor').as_posix(): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in (HERE / 'native/vendor').rglob('*') if p.is_file()}

+        need(receipt['word_sha256'] == hashlib.sha256((HERE / 'inputs' / f'NEW-{tag}.json.gz').read_bytes()).hexdigest(), 'native input')

+        need([s['step'] for s in receipt['steps']] == ['native', 'ledgers', 'local-replay', 'wrappers', 'phases'] and all(s['exit_code'] == 0 for s in receipt['steps']), 'native stages')
+        rows[tag] = {'local_profile': word['report']['local_profile'], 'width_inventory': word['report']['width_inventory'], 'staged_entrances': [e['helper'] for e in record['entrances']]}

+
